model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percentage) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME—across varying co-occurrence numbers, with the x-axis representing the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000. The y-axis shows the accuracy percentage, ranging from 40% to 65%. The Base method, represented by a black line with circle markers, starts at approximately 39% accuracy and increases gradually to about 44% as the co-occurrence number increases. The MEND method, shown with a brown line and diamond markers, begins at around 44% and rises steadily to approximately 56% at the highest co-occurrence number. The FT method, depicted by a blue line with triangle markers, starts at about 40% and increases to roughly 48%. The MEMIT method, represented by a purple line with square markers, begins at approximately 43% and increases to about 55%. The ROME method, shown with a green line and square markers, starts at around 51% and shows the most significant increase, reaching approximately 66% at the highest co-occurrence number. Overall, all methods exhibit an upward trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases, with ROME consistently achieving the highest accuracy across the range.
